hormuz_disruption.label: Iran / Hormuz Disruption
hormuz_disruption.last_note: Iran re-escalated on June 20 citing Israeli violations of the June 17 MOU, CENTCOM counters that traffic is still flowing but clandestine flows represent only 2.9M bpd versus pre-war 15.6M bpd, and Switzerland talks on June 22 are the single credible off-ramp — closure risk is structurally entrenched not fading.

stagflation_regime.label: Stagflation Regime
stagflation_regime.last_note: BLS confirmed May 2026 CPI at 4.2 percent YoY with the Fed holding at 3.50 to 3.75 percent and explicitly citing energy supply shocks as the cause; the FOMC now signals a possible hike by October while GDP grows at 2.0 percent, the textbook stagflation configuration.

ai_bubble_risk.label: AI Bubble Risk Q4 2026
ai_bubble_risk.last_note: Hyperscaler capex is confirmed at $725 billion for 2026 with capital intensity at 45 to 57 percent of revenue and Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan projecting $1.5 trillion in new tech sector debt over three years, but Microsoft Azure backlog of $80 billion is power-constrained not demand-constrained, keeping the overbuild thesis unresolved.

gold_supercycle.label: Gold Supercycle
gold_supercycle.last_note: Gold is pinned at an intraday floor near $4,170/oz, caught between the 200-day moving average and the 50-day moving average, while central bank net purchases collapsed to only 16 tons in Q1 2026 and JPMorgan notes growing fears that the Fed may hike into energy-driven inflation, suppressing gold momentum even as JPMorgan maintains a $6,000/oz year-end target.

copper_deficit.label: Structural Copper Deficit
copper_deficit.last_note: Spot treatment charges fell to minus $70 per ton by late March 2026 confirming extreme concentrate tightness, JPMorgan forecasts a refined copper deficit of 330,000 tons in 2026, and S&P Global projects a cumulative deficit of 3 million tonnes by 2036; the structural thesis is intact even as near-term macro resistance creates volatility.

nuclear_renaissance.label: Nuclear Renaissance
nuclear_renaissance.last_note: Energy requirements for AI data centers are on track to double global data center electricity consumption between 2022 and 2026 per IEA, Microsoft Azure has $80 billion in unfulfilled orders due to power constraints not demand softness, and Sprott sees renewed contracting and pivotal US policy decisions boosting uranium demand in 2026 as SMR construction has broken ground at Darlington.

ALAB.note: ALAB posted record Q1 2026 revenue of $308.4 million up 93 percent YoY confirming the AI connectivity thesis is operationally intact, but the AVOID signal reflects a P/E of 104.51 at a moment when the Nasdaq is down 1.32 percent and rising 10Y yields at 4.509 percent compress high-multiple growth names hardest — the business thesis is valid but the valuation entry is not.

POWL.note: Hyperscaler capex confirmed at $725 billion for 2026 with power constraints cited as the primary bottleneck on Azure fulfillment, which directly supports POWL switchgear demand, but the P/E of 44.77 and rising 10Y yields make the risk-reward binary on whether data center buildout timelines hold.

MOD.note: The AI liquid cooling thesis remains structurally valid as GPU density and data center power loads scale, but MOD carries negative FCF of minus $101 million while interest rates are rising and the 10Y yield moved up 1.30 percent today, making the negative FCF profile a material financing risk not yet resolved.

GFS.note: GFS 2026 design win momentum and record backlog remain intact but the company is exposed to hyperscaler debt-financed capex cycles; if AI monetisation disappoints and hyperscalers pull back, GFS advanced node demand is first to be deferred given its position in the mid-tier foundry market rather than the leading-edge TSMC tier.

CRDO.note: The DustPhotonics acquisition brings silicon photonics PICs in-house, CRDO expects optical revenues to exceed $500 million in fiscal 2027, and the 800G ZF optical transceiver launch positions CRDO ahead of the AI cluster scaling curve — the thesis has strengthened not drifted.

ARM.note: ARM trades at a P/E of 132.2 with hyperscalers now funding AI capex via $1.5 trillion in projected debt issuance; if AI monetisation disappoints and capex is trimmed, ARM royalty growth stalls while its valuation offers zero margin of safety against a Nasdaq correction already underway.

S.note: SentinelOne cut 8 percent of its workforce and issued lackluster guidance, signaling margin pressure is structural not cyclical; the WATCH thesis requires evidence of ARR reacceleration that has not yet materialized, making the cybersecurity thesis valid but the vehicle broken.

ZS.note: Zscaler has the strongest FCF in cybersecurity at $1.1 billion but the AVOID signal reflects valuation compression risk at P/E of 26.98 as rising 10Y yields at 4.509 percent systematically reprice long-duration growth assets; FCF strength does not offset duration risk in the current macro regime.

AXON.note: AXON Q1 2026 revenue of $807 million up 34 percent with ARR at $1.5 billion growing 35 percent, AI products up over 700 percent, and full-year FCF guided to approximately $450 million — the prior AVOID call based on $63 million FCF is now broken and thesis drift is STRONGLY POSITIVE, warranting immediate re-evaluation to WATCH or BUY.

ISRG.note: Intuitive Surgical has zero debt, $4.5B cash, 23% revenue growth, and $2.3B FCF making it a genuine compounder, but at 36x forward earnings and 29.4% below highs the surgical robotics moat thesis is unchanged — the drift is purely valuation-related, not fundamental, and the stock remains a hold-not-add until the multiple contracts further.

RXRX.note: Recursion Pharmaceuticals has revenue growth of minus 56.1%, is burning $178M in FCF with negative operating margins of minus 1985%, and is 55.2% below its 52-week high — the original AI drug discovery thesis has collapsed as clinical pipeline progress has not justified the technology premium and this is now a capital destruction story with no near-term catalyst.

JEDI.note: The drone and modern warfare rearmament thesis is structurally intact given the Hormuz crisis has accelerated defense technology procurement, but at 25% below highs and with no fundamental data available for an ETF wrapper this remains a theme trade that requires a defined technical base before adding risk.

CWAN.note: Clearwater Analytics has 74.4% revenue growth and $160M FCF which is operationally compelling, but analyst targets of $24.47 to $24.55 against the current $24.35 price provide virtually zero upside consensus — at PEG of 10.24 and EV/EBITDA of 73.69 the institutional fintech thesis is fully priced with no margin of safety.

GRAB.note: Grab at $3.30 with $6.5B cash, 23.5% revenue growth, and PEG of 0.87 is the most asymmetric deep value setup in the portfolio on a pure fundamentals basis, but the stock is 50.2% below highs and the Southeast Asia super-app monetization thesis requires a specific catalyst such as a buyback announcement or profitability upgrade to unlock value — thesis intact, no trigger yet.

VRT.note: Vertiv is a direct beneficiary of the above 1 trillion dollar 2026 data center capex cycle with power constraint urgency confirmed by the Microsoft 80 billion dollar Azure backlog, but stretched valuation demands flawless execution at a time when macro uncertainty is high.

MU.note: MU led the chip stock rally on June 15 on Iran deal optimism and structural AI memory demand is intact given that memory cost inflation drove data center capex higher in Q1 2026, but the stock is cyclical and a stagflation-driven consumer slowdown could compress DRAM pricing outside the AI data center vertical.

AMD.note: AMD surged on June 15 following an analyst upgrade and the Iran deal catalyst, with the company announcing up to 2 billion pounds in UK AI investment and the MEXT memory optimization acquisition signaling a serious data center strategy, but the stock at 548.80 dollars trades at a premium that assumes continued hyperscaler GPU wallet share gains from Nvidia.
